design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DESIGN DOSSIER — benefit_and_tax_appeals task 0 (category appeal).

[Step 0 — draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 5]. The tree has one prerequisite problem; appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting takes 5 factors and appeal_ext_video_session takes 5.

[Why this is a good test] A Deaf claimant asks for one thing: her appeal hearing held by video. The surface goal names no number and no prerequisite. To serve it the agent must (1) read the video-session policy and see that on an appeal at filed status a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record; (2) find in find_appeals that the appeal 55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939 is still status filed with an empty hearing_date, so that state does not hold; (3) work out from the first-hearing-setting policy (the only write in this difficulty that records a first/initial hearing setting) that the office must first docket the appeal and set the first telephone hearing; (4) compute that hearing date from five rules over the appeal's filing record, the claim's payment and certification history (another difficulty), the interpreter request, the open subpoena and the claim's federal program; (5) compute the video session date from the set date plus four record-driven gaps and the docket's video calendar day; (6) hand the booking to the claimant, because the video election is the party's own act. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling history across the appeal and claim/identity products, and arithmetic with a weekday rule — not from missing information or tool guessing (each problem has exactly one target tool).

[Scope budget] Already occupied: nothing (first task). This task claims appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting (docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da) and appeal_ext_video_session (book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f). Reserved for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5, 6]): the reopening of a dismissed appeal with its reopened telephone setting (appeal_reopened, agent) and the party's in-person session booking (appeal_hearing_scheduled, user) — independent policies, tools, docket (Employer Contribution Rate) and customer type (employer); nothing of task 0 is reused.

[Problem-tree card]
root problem: appeal_ext_video_session (owner=user tool book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f).
edge: appeal_ext_video_session -> appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting; kind value_input; gate video_set_days; form state.
prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, in the video-session rule): "On an appeal at filed status, a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after" joining this policy's result (booking the video session) to what it waits on; rewrites exactly as "On an appeal at filed status, a video session is not booked until the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record"; (2) XX is a record-visible state (status scheduled plus an appeal_hearing_scheduled record with schedule_reason initial), named in business words; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) hard requirement ("only after"), scope = appeals at filed status, the same scope and strength as the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty records a first (initial) hearing setting: the docketing write of appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting (the reopening write records a 'reopening' setting, the party's mode-change bookings record no schedule reason). Derivation: sentence + find_appeals (status filed, hearing_date empty, no hearing-setting record in find_appeal_events) + the first-hearing-setting rule ("When the appeals office dockets an appeal filed on a docket that holds hearings, it sets the first hearing by telephone ...") -> the one resolving action is docketing the appeal with its first hearing.
condition: the appeal carries an initial hearing setting, status scheduled, appeals.hearing_date set.
unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.appeals.55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939.status = filed; initial_state.appeals.55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939.hearing_date = '' ; appeal_events holds only the interpreter request 39d748db-1f09-44cf-844a-e5eb19850b66 and two exhibits — no hearing setting.
resolving action: docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da (owner agent), synchronous, same frozen_time.
topological order: appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting -> appeal_ext_video_session (single chain, no parallel edges).
deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the docketing write leaves hearing_date empty, so video_set_days cannot be evaluated (the recompute raises: raises: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '') — there is no set date to count the video session from; in the terminal DB the appeal stays status filed with no initial setting row, so the hash differs from gold in any case.
no user hint: user_scenario asks only for a video hearing; it never names docketing, a first setting, a telephone hearing or any order of steps; the fact "no hearing notice has come" is given only if asked and is true in initial_state (hearing_date empty).
tools do not block: book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f writes its setting and moves hearing_date whatever the appeal's status or prior settings; docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da never checks anything but writes the setting and status.
owner=user problem: the video election and booking is the party's own choice about how it takes part in its hearing (base appeal_evt_scheduling lets a party ask for another mode); the agent unlocks and hands it over after the docketing write; the claimant runs it on the spot with the docket number and day count the agent gives.

[Base-invariant card]
- Subject appeal_docketed / appeal_hearing_scheduled, governed by appeal_evt_scheduling (gate hearing_on_open_appeal: "A hearing is set only while the appeal status is filed, scheduled or dismissed."; evidence appeals.appeal_id/appeals.status of 55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939; status filed at the docketing step, scheduled at the video step) and appeal_agg_linked_dockets (no gate applies to these subjects — policy_scope: no linked appeal of the same parties exists; find_appeals returns only 55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939).
- No time gate applies to these subjects. Filing timeliness is already settled: mailed 2026-09-25, docket deadline 21 days -> 2026-10-16; postmark 2026-10-02 is in time, late_filing_reason none.
- Overwrites declared (see rework round 2 for the postponement clauses): appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting replaces the base sentence "The first hearing is set within the docket's scheduling target after filing, ..." (the leads can move the first hearing past the target); appeal_ext_video_session replaces the base mode sentence by one that adds the video hearing on request. Every other base clause (notice minimum, interested parties, phone registration, written argument) stays in force.

[Business-object card] Target object: appeal 55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939 (Separation Issue docket, appellant claimant 99c79b5a-4879-49c6-906c-36d5df6daa2d, determination_record_id = claim b612832c-a2e4-49c7-940a-d4111683bc20). Rows entering aggregates: appeal_events interpreter 39d748db-1f09-44cf-844a-e5eb19850b66; exhibits 1bb4a0b8-c8c2-40fb-869e-612005e7b276, efd27c53-1192-41d9-a6bf-2337014d8cba; appeal_requests subpoena 6e95b438-7b02-4d20-90a7-033ac775d8ef; claim_certifications 10 rows (9 inside the window); claim_ledger 2 rows (no payment); idv case ca24e9de-5edd-4a5a-a7fa-f72f31fab17f. Excluded by rule: certification of 2026-08-10 (outside two months), the waiting-week row (not a payment). No reversal/compensation rows exist. Both writes carry appeal_id, the narrowest key.

[Factor cards — appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting] first_setting_clock (method): the appeal row shows filing_channel=mail, late_filing_reason=none, filed_date=2026-10-02 (postmark), so the tier 'no late-filing reason, filed by mail' applies — the clock starts on the presumed receipt date, mail_receipt_days=3 after the postmark (2026-10-05), first_clock_offset = 3 - 12 = -9 days from today; the baseline (clock from the filing date, offset -12) gives result 29. first_setting_target (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty claim): claim_ledger for claim b612832c-a2e4-49c7-940a-d4111683bc20 holds no claim_benefit_paid row at all (the 2026-08-04 claim_waiting_week_served row is not a payment), so recent_payments=0; claim_certifications show 9 weeks certified on dates later than 2026-08-14 (2026-08-17 … 2026-10-12; the 2026-08-10 certification is outside the window), so recent_certified_weeks=9 >= expedite_min_weeks 3 — tier 1, expedited_target_days=14; the baseline (docket scheduling target 30 for the Separation Issue docket) gives result 48. first_setting_interpreter_lead (parameter): the latest (only) interpreter request on the appeal (appeal_events 39d748db-1f09-44cf-844a-e5eb19850b66, 2026-10-05) is american_sign_language — tier 1, sign_language_lead_days=10; the baseline (0) gives result 22. first_setting_subpoena_lead (parameter): one subpoena request stands received and undecided (appeal_requests 6e95b438-7b02-4d20-90a7-033ac775d8ef) — tier 2, one_subpoena_lead_days=7; the baseline (0) gives result 26. first_setting_federal_records_lead (parameter, cross-difficulty claim): the appealed claim b612832c-a2e4-49c7-940a-d4111683bc20 is an Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) claim — tier 1, federal_employee_records_days=10; the baseline (0) gives result 22. first_hearing_offset (plumbing + notice-minimum guard): MX(7, -9 + 14 + 10 + 7 + 10) = 32; the guard does not bite. first_hearing_weekday / result (weekend rule of the baseline): 2026-10-14 + 32 = 2026-11-15, a Sunday (weekday index 6), so the first hearing moves to Monday 2026-11-16; notice_period_days = 33. All-baseline fall-back (computation document only): clock from filing (-12) + target 30 = 18 -> 2026-11-01 Sunday -> 19 = 19 (differs from 33). Near-misses: the waiting-week ledger row (a careless reader counts it as a payment and drops to the docket target), the 2026-08-10 certification (outside the window), the postmark date (counting the clock from it instead of presumed receipt).

[Factor cards — appeal_ext_video_session] video_set_days (value_input from the first hearing setting): after the docketing write the appeal's hearing_date is 2026-11-16, 33 days from today. video_block_gap (parameter, multi-source): latest interpreter request american_sign_language (not Spanish) AND the Separation Issue docket's hearing_length_minutes 60 >= long_hearing_minutes 60 — tier 1, long_video_block_days=10; the baseline (standard 5) gives result 55. video_accommodation_review (parameter, multi-source): latest interpreter request american_sign_language AND one medical_statement exhibit received (appeal_events 1bb4a0b8-c8c2-40fb-869e-612005e7b276, 2026-10-07) — tier 1, sign_language_review_days=5; the baseline (0) gives result 55. video_identity_check (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty idv): idv_cases ca24e9de-5edd-4a5a-a7fa-f72f31fab17f on the appealed claim stands verified through In-Person Proofing — American Job Center (not a Video Trusted Referee Session) — tier 2, other_pathway_identity_check_days=3; the baseline (0) gives result 55. video_exhibit_preparation (parameter): two exhibits submitted by the claimant appellant stand received (1bb4a0b8-c8c2-40fb-869e-612005e7b276 medical_statement, efd27c53-1192-41d9-a6bf-2337014d8cba written_statement) — tier 1, two_exhibit_preparation_days=5; the baseline (0) gives result 55. video_candidate_days (plumbing): 33 + 10 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 56, i.e. Wednesday 2026-12-09. video_calendar_day (method): the appeal is on the Separation Issue docket — tier 1, the session moves to the first Tuesday or Thursday on or after 2026-12-09, i.e. Thursday 2026-12-10 (+1); the baseline (weekend rule only) leaves Wednesday 2026-12-09 and gives result 56. result: 56 + 1 = 57 (video session on 2026-12-10). All-baseline fall-back: 33 + 5 = 38 -> 2026-11-21 Saturday -> Monday 2026-11-23 = 40 (differs from 57). Near-misses: the identity case is verified (a reader who sees 'verified' and stops gives 0 days, but the pathway is not a video trusted referee); counting only medical exhibits as 'exhibits' (1 -> 3 days instead of 5).

[Seed rationale] customers (identity grounding); claims b612832c-a2e4-49c7-940a-d4111683bc20 UCFE active, hold released when the separation determination was recorded (hold_reason none, no payment since the waiting week); claim_ledger entitlement + waiting week (history window evidence, near-miss); claim_certifications 10 weekly online certifications, all timely (the claimant keeps certifying while appealing, as continue_certifying_required demands); idv_cases verified in person at an American Job Center (identity check tier); appeals row status filed, mailed appeal; appeal_events interpreter ASL + two timely exhibits; appeal_requests one received subpoena (coworker witness). Removing any of: the certifications (target tier falls to priority 21 -> different result), the interpreter row (lead 0 and block gap 5), the subpoena (lead 0), the idv case (identity days 0), an exhibit (prep days 3) changes a scored value. Automatic clauses checked: no hold to release, no week to pay (determination disqualified the weeks), no appeal deadline pending, no recovery to suspend; nothing ignites an obligation outside the tree.

[Persona] Natural, relay-typed voice; volunteers only the surface goal (video hearing) and why (Deaf, interpreter must see her). Identity, filing channel, interpreter request, absence of a hearing notice, equipment, and preference against in-person are given only when asked. Passive reactions: agrees if told something must be done on the Department's side first; runs the booking exactly as handed over; closes after reading back the booked date. She asks nothing else.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone, SSN last4, ZIP) -> find_appeals -> find_appeal_events -> find_appeal_requests -> find_claims -> find_claim_ledger -> find_claim_certifications -> find_idv_cases -> unlock+call docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da(appeal_id=55ade028-0828-4c34-9edf-7d7090a68939, notice_period_days=33) -> unlock book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f and hand it to the claimant -> claimant calls it with session_days=57.

[Verification code] An authoring script (removed from the bundle after use) replayed the gold writes with the real tools and evaluated each compute with the COMPUTE gate's own engine (build_env/eval_compute/substitute) at handling time; check_compute.py reproduces every figure below (run: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0049_state_unemployment_insurance_agency/tasks/benefit_and_tax_appeals). Output: first setting result=33, per-factor baselines {'first_setting_clock': 29, 'first_setting_target': 48, 'first_setting_interpreter_lead': 22, 'first_setting_subpoena_lead': 26, 'first_setting_federal_records_lead': 22}, baseline_result=19; video session result=57, per-factor baselines {'video_block_gap': 55, 'video_accommodation_review': 55, 'video_identity_check': 55, 'video_exhibit_preparation': 55, 'video_calendar_day': 56}, baseline_result=40; video without the first setting: raises: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> GT call -> terminal state: appeal_ext_first_hearing_setting -> docket_appeal_hearing_a28520da -> step 10 -> appeal status scheduled, hearing_date 2026-11-16, initial telephone setting row; appeal_ext_video_session -> book_video_hearing_session_16bf8e4f -> step 12 -> video setting row 2026-12-10 13:00 (a change of hearing mode: schedule_reason not_applicable, requested_by claimant), hearing_date 2026-12-10. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = [first, video].

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Using only the two policies' prose, the tool schemas, the persona's lines and the find_* returns: the appeal is filed with no hearing -> the video rule's prerequisite fails -> docket first: clock from presumed receipt 2026-10-05, expedited 14 (no payments, 9 certified weeks), +10 ASL, +7 one open subpoena, +10 UCFE = 2026-11-15 Sunday -> 2026-11-16 (33 days); video: +10 +5 +3 +5 = 2026-12-09 Wednesday -> Thursday 2026-12-10 (57 days). Agrees with gold.


[Rework round 2 — policy-task audit items]
G1 (undeclared postponement override): the video rule now states the session is "a change of hearing mode made at that party's request" and that such a change "is not a postponement: it needs no postponement request or decision, is not subject to the postponement lead time, does not count toward the party's postponements and is not held to the reschedule window"; appeal_evt_postponement joined base_policy_refs and (as narrowed in round 3) its clause defining a postponement request is declared superseded in overwrite; the video tool now records schedule_reason not_applicable instead of postponement (also closes O8). The scored 57 is now the only reading: the mode change is declared not to be a postponement.
G2 (first_setting_target tier collision): priority_target_days 21 -> 18, distinct from every docket's scheduling target (21/30/45/60) and from the expedited 14. This world takes the expedited tier, so every figure is unchanged (33; baselines 29/48/22/26/22; fall-back 19).
G4 (identity read): the rule now reads the appellant's own identity verification case on the appealed claim, exactly what the compute's customer-scoped read returns; here the appellant is the claimant who owns case ca24e9de-5edd-4a5a-a7fa-f72f31fab17f, so the tier (verified elsewhere, 3 days) is unchanged.
G5 (sentence broader than condition): the prerequisite sentence now reads "On an appeal at filed status, a video session is booked only after the appeal stands at scheduled status with its first hearing setting on record." and the condition carries the same status and scope; a separate scope sentence ("A video session is booked only for an appeal that stands at filed or scheduled status.") keeps dismissed appeals out of the video rule, so a missed past hearing date can no longer be the base of a video date. On a filed appeal exactly one write (the first docketing) brings the stated state about.
O6: video_identity_check.cross_difficulty set to null (idv is cross-category, not a difficulty); the task's cross-difficulty factors remain first_setting_target and first_setting_federal_records_lead (claim).
O7: "weekly benefit payment" -> "benefit payment" in the first-setting rule and ladders, matching the compute's count of every claim_benefit_paid row.
Persona observation: the unconditional line pre-clearing unnamed Department writes was removed; the conditional "If the agent explains that something has to be done on the Department's side ..." remains.
Re-verification (engine replay after the rework): first setting 33, video 57, per-factor and fall-back figures identical to the round-1 figures above; skipping the docketing still leaves no hearing date to count from.

[Rework round 3 — policy-KB audit, source-side items]
Postponement overwrite narrowed (supersedes the round-2 wording above, which said the lead-time, per-party-maximum and reschedule-window sentences were declared superseded): those three base sentences are no longer retired and keep governing genuine postponements. The only base clause the video policy now overrides from appeal_evt_postponement is "A party may ask to postpone a set hearing.", replaced by the video rule's sentence "A party may ask to postpone a set hearing, and the postponement rules, with their lead time, per-party maximum and reschedule window, govern that request; a party's request to hold its set hearing as a video session instead is a change of hearing mode and is not a request to postpone." The explanatory sentence "A change of hearing mode booked as a video session is not a postponement: ..." stays. The scored reading is unchanged (the base postponement rules do not reach a mode change), so all figures stand: first setting 33 (baselines 29/48/22/26/22, fall-back 19), video 57 (55/55/55/55/56, fall-back 40). No tool name, signature or docstring changed.
user_scenario: You are Delphine Marchetti-Okafor, 47, a former mail processing clerk at the United States Postal Service plant in Sun Prairie who was let go in late July. You are Deaf and you are typing through a text relay service, so your messages are short, plain and a little blunt; you apologise once for the relay delay and then get on with it. Open by saying you appealed the decision that denied your unemployment benefits and that you need your appeal hearing to be held by video hearing, because a telephone hearing does not work for you and your sign language interpreter has to be able to see you. That is the whole reason you are calling: you want the hearing on your appeal to be a video hearing. Only if the agent asks how you filed, say you mailed the appeal letter on October 2. Only if the agent asks whether you already asked for an interpreter, say yes, you asked for an American Sign Language interpreter in writing. You do not know any docket or reference number for the appeal; if asked, say you have not received any letter with a number on it yet, and ask the agent to look it up. Only if the agent asks whether you have received a hearing notice or a hearing date, say no, nothing has come in the mail. Give your identity details only when the agent asks for them, one or two at a time as asked: your phone number is 6085553417, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 3582, your ZIP code is 53748, your date of birth is March 22, 1979, and your email is delphine.marchettiokafor@lakemail.net. If the agent asks whether you can take part in a video hearing, say yes, you have a laptop with a camera and good internet at home. If the agent asks whether you would rather come in person, say no, you want video. If the agent asks about other accommodations or documents, say your audiologist's letter and your written statement were already mailed in and you have nothing else to send. If the agent explains that something has to be done on the Department's side before the video session can be booked, tell them that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent tells you that you can book the video session yourself and hands you the booking, use exactly the appeal docket number and the number of days the agent gives you; do not change them. Once the booking comes back showing the video session date, read the date back, thank the agent and end the conversation. If the agent says the video session is booked, you are satisfied and say goodbye. You do not ask about the outcome of the appeal, your benefits, or anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single chain (one edge, no parallel prerequisites). The order is fixed by the prerequisite sentence: the video session is counted from the set hearing date, which exists only after the docketing write; the reverse order leaves the video formula without a set date and the docketing would then overwrite the booked date.
